description: USB 2.0 full-speed to UART bridge, internal clock (no crystal), modem signals, 5 V or 3.3 V supply (SOP-16)

package.name: SOP-16
package.page: 3. Package: SOP-16, 3.9 mm (150 mil) body, 1.27 mm pitch; the datasheet has no drawing

pins.name: TXD
pins.description: UART data out (to the MCU's RX); idle high

pins.name: RXD
pins.description: UART data in (from the MCU's TX); internal pull-up

pins.name: V3
pins.description: internal 3.3 V regulator node: 100 nF to GND at 5 V, tied to VCC at 3.3 V

pins.name: UD+
pins.description: USB D+, straight to the connector (no series resistor, internal pull-up)

pins.name: UD-
pins.description: USB D-, straight to the connector

pins.name: NC
pins.description: empty pin on CH340C: leave open

pins.name: OUT#
pins.description: modem general output, active low (on newer lots a 4.7 kohm pull-down turns it into a second, open-drain DTR#)

pins.name: CTS#
pins.description: clear to send, active low; pulled up inside: may stay open

pins.name: DSR#
pins.description: data set ready, active low; pulled up inside: may stay open

pins.name: RI#
pins.description: ring indicator, active low; pulled up inside: may stay open

pins.name: DCD#
pins.description: carrier detect, active low; pulled up inside: may stay open

pins.name: DTR#
pins.description: data terminal ready, active low (auto-reset of an MCU through 100 nF)

pins.name: R232
pins.description: auxiliary RS232 enable (inverts RXD) when high; pulled down inside: may stay open

recommended.what: VCC (3.1-3.6 V with V3 tied to VCC, 4.0-5.3 V with V3 decoupled)

parameters.conditions: Total power supply current during operation, VCC = 5 V, TA = 25 degC, USB bus pins excluded; at VCC = V3 = 3.3 V the datasheet gives 4 mA typ / 12 mA max (section 6.3)

source.location: p. 8, section 6.2 5V Electrical Parameters, ICC (total supply current during operation) row

parts.rating: at 5 V; at 3.3 V V3 joins VCC as well

notes: No crystal: the CH340C has an internal clock (baud rate error under 1.8 %).
UD+ and UD- go straight to the USB connector: the part has its USB pull-up and needs no series resistors.
support.page: 5.1 Clock, reset, power; 7.1 and 7.6 application circuits

notes: At 5 V: VCC from VBUS, V3 decoupled with 100 nF, and the UART lines swing to 5 V. At 3.3 V: V3 tied to VCC, both on the 3.3 V rail, logic at 3.3 V.
Unused modem inputs (CTS#, DSR#, RI#, DCD#) have pull-ups and may stay open; R232 has a pull-down and stays open.
Arduino-style auto-reset: DTR# through 100 nF to the MCU's reset (with the reset pull-up); ESP32 auto-boot: DTR# and RTS# through two transistors to EN and GPIO0.
Keep the decoupling capacitors next to pins 16 and 4 and route D+/D- as a pair.

pins.source: WCH datasheet CH340DS1 version 3D, section 4 (pins, SOP16 column), 5.1 and 6 (parameters)
